detailed_description: The CSS Filter Generator helps you build a single CSS filter declaration with a browser preview. Use presets such as grayscale, sepia, vintage, dramatic, faded, or inverted, then adjust sliders for blur, brightness, contrast, grayscale, hue-rotate, invert, saturate, sepia, and opacity. The preview applies the current filter to a default image or to an image you upload, and the output panel shows the ready filter property for copying. This is useful for quickly prototyping image effects, hover states, muted thumbnails, or simple visual treatments before moving the CSS into a project.
usage_steps: Choose a preset or start from the default unfiltered state.
Optionally upload an image to replace the default preview image.
Adjust the sliders for blur, brightness, contrast, grayscale, hue rotation, invert, saturate, sepia, and opacity.
Review the image preview as the filter changes.
Click Copy CSS to copy the filter declaration.
usage_examples: A front-end developer tests a muted thumbnail style with grayscale and lower opacity.
A designer previews a vintage image treatment with sepia, contrast, and brightness adjustments.
An e-commerce team creates a simple hover effect by increasing saturation and contrast.
A blogger copies a CSS filter declaration for styling article images.
